USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

The aluminum burden in renal failure

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 71-year-old patient receiving dialysis has used sucralfate and an aluminum-containing antacid for several months. Progressive bone pain and cognitive changes prompt a review of nonprescription medicines. Which drug-related accumulation is especially concerning given the patient’s impaired renal elimination?

  1. Potassium
  2. Bismuth
  3. Iron
  4. Iodide
  5. Aluminum
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Aluminum

Renal impairment reduces elimination of absorbed aluminum; sucralfate plus aluminum antacids increases the burden.

Understanding the options

Aluminum
Renal impairment reduces elimination of absorbed aluminum; sucralfate plus aluminum antacids increases the burden.
Potassium
Sucralfate does not supply a substantial potassium load.
Bismuth
Bismuth is present in different ulcer medications.
Iron
Iron is not the metal component of sucralfate.
Iodide
Iodide is not the relevant constituent.
